assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology led to incretin-based drugs that now transform treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity, with cardiovascular and renal benefits; a rare complete arc from hormone biology to a major therapeutic class with enormous patient impact.
assessment.attribution: Holst (GLP-1 biology and secretion in humans) and Drucker (GLP-1 and GLP-2 actions, proglucagon biology, translation) are the core physiological contributors; Knudsen represents the pharmaceutical design of long-acting analogues. Mojsov's early characterisation of the active peptide and the roles of others not on this list are contested, so the allocation is not fully clean.
assessment.maturity: Mature: multiple large randomised outcome trials, regulatory approvals and widespread clinical use over more than a decade; recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Fair allocation among Drucker, Holst, Mojsov and Knudsen, and omitted pioneers, is unresolved; I have not independently verified priority claims.
Whether the committee prefers to honour physiology or the drug-development component.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells with chimeric antigen receptors have produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and opened a new therapeutic modality, with clear originality and broad clinical impact.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain and June both drove the design of costimulated CARs and their clinical translation in leukaemia and lymphoma; Rosenberg contributed adoptive cell therapy and early gene-engineered T-cell trials, but the credited names do not include Eshhar, a likely early originator of the CAR concept, so the fair configuration is uncertain.
assessment.maturity: Strong: several approved products, long follow-up for some patients and independent confirmation; long-term safety, solid-tumour efficacy and access remain limitations.
uncertainties: Omission of the original chimeric-receptor concept originators in the supplied credit.
Durability beyond several years and secondary malignancy risk are still being defined.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response defined a new mode of organelle-to-nucleus signalling and is central to proteostasis, secretory-cell physiology and many diseases; conceptually original and foundational.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori independently and jointly identified the Ire1/Hac1 (XBP1) and transcriptional signalling arms, a compact and well-defined pair; other contributors such as Kozutsumi or Ron/Harding on PERK are not in the credited set.
assessment.maturity: Very mature: decades of independent confirmation, extensive follow-up in disease and drug development, and long-standing recognition including the Lasker Award.
uncertainties: Direct disease-treatment impact is more limited than the conceptual impact.
Whether PERK/ATF6 arm contributors should share recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Virus-like particle HPV vaccines prevent persistent infection, cervical precancer and cancer, and population data now show large reductions in disease: a major preventive-medicine achievement.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller developed the L1 VLP technology at NCI; Frazer contributed VLP vaccine development and the Gardasil project. Allocation with other groups, including Zhou and companies, is disputed and I cannot resolve it from the supplied text.
assessment.maturity: Mature: population-level effectiveness data, including cancer incidence reductions, have been independently confirmed across countries.
uncertainties: Priority disputes over VLP formation across several laboratories.
Whether recognition should favour basic virology or vaccine development.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience causal, cell-type-specific control of activity and has transformed circuit research, with early therapeutic uses such as vision restoration emerging.
assessment.attribution: Nagel and Hegemann (with Bamberg) identified and characterised channelrhodopsin function; Deisseroth, Boyden and Miesenböck established neuronal control and applications. At most three can be proposed and several strong contributors would be excluded.
assessment.maturity: Methodologically mature and widely replicated, but clinical translation remains early.
uncertainties: Crowded credit set of six; a three-person limit leaves out Boyden, Bamberg and Miesenböck.
Impact is primarily as a research tool rather than a medical treatment.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Antisense correction of SMN2 splicing yielded nusinersen, the first effective therapy for spinal muscular atrophy, with a clear mechanistic discovery and dramatic clinical effect in infants.
assessment.attribution: Krainer identified the splicing mechanism and target region for correction, while Bennett led antisense oligonucleotide chemistry and development; this two-person configuration is coherent, although collaborators such as Hua may contribute.
assessment.maturity: Reasonably mature: approved since 2016 with long-term data, though other SMA therapies (gene replacement, small molecules) complicate the picture.
uncertainties: Broader antisense-oligonucleotide platform contributions may need separate recognition.
Long-term durability data continue to accrue.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imatinib and BCR-ABL inhibition established the paradigm of molecularly targeted cancer therapy and converted chronic myeloid leukaemia into a manageable chronic disease.
assessment.attribution: Lydon (compound discovery), Druker (clinical proof of concept) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and second-generation inhibitors) form a plausible trio; the earlier BCR-ABL gene discovery by others is not in this credited set and has partly been recognised previously.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, with long-term survival data and wide replication; recognition could be seen as somewhat overdue.
uncertainties: Relation to prior Nobel-recognised oncogene work and the Lasker awardees' overlap.
Whether the trio fairly omits chemistry contributors at Ciba-Geigy.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Adult stem-cell-derived organoids established self-organising three-dimensional epithelial culture from Lgr5 stem cells, enabling disease modelling, drug testing and personalised medicine research.
assessment.attribution: Clevers led the Lgr5 stem cell and organoid work; Sato carried out the key first culture. The configuration is clean, though organoid methods from pluripotent stem cells are separate.
assessment.maturity: Reasonably mature and widely adopted, but clinical translation is still developing and some applications are premature.
uncertainties: Clinical impact so far is modest relative to research impact.
Overlap with pluripotent-stem-cell organoid approaches not credited here.
